records.mechanism_summary: Review-level synthesis describes mitochondrial and lysosomal dysfunction as amplifiers of proteotoxic stress in Alzheimer disease. M-to-Pr is retained only as a directional hypothesis because metabolic impairment may alter energy-dependent protein clearance; lysosomal and proteostasis subdomains must be operationally separated.

references.title: Toward a Unified Framework in Molecular Neurobiology of Alzheimer's Disease: Revisiting the Pathophysiological Hypotheses
Mechanisms of autophagy-lysosome dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases

records.limitations: Review-level mechanistic synthesis, not a longitudinal causal estimate. M and Pr require non-overlapping operational definitions. No sign or coefficient is assigned.

records.mechanism_summary: Neuroinflammation is described as a central hub connecting amyloid, tau, and vascular factors, while proteostasis, inflammation, and metabolic pathways are presented as interacting systems. The direction and temporal ordering between I and Pr remain unresolved in this record.

references.title: Toward a Unified Framework in Molecular Neurobiology of Alzheimer's Disease: Revisiting the Pathophysiological Hypotheses
Systems biology of Alzheimer's Disease: a scoping review of key pathways and mechanisms

records.limitations: A hub or pathway interaction does not establish a directed edge. The 2026 scoping review reports heterogeneous evidence maturity across pathways; this record must not be converted into a directed parameter.

records.mechanism_summary: Parkinson disease reviews describe linked mitochondrial oxidative stress and lysosomal dysfunction in a pathogenic feedback cycle involving oxidized dopamine and alpha-synuclein. Impaired lysosomal activity can also compromise protein processing and mitophagy, supporting reciprocal candidate hypotheses between M and Pr.

records.limitations: The feedback is a mechanistic synthesis across genetic, cellular, and experimental evidence. It does not determine patient-specific edge strength, timing, sign, or whether the same relationship applies to every Parkinson subtype.

records.mechanism_summary: A Parkinson disease review describes alpha-synuclein acting as a damage-associated molecular pattern that can engage pattern-recognition receptors on microglia and initiate innate immune signaling. This supports a provisional Pr-to-I mechanism hypothesis.

references.title: Parkinson Disease Signaling Pathways, Molecular Mechanisms, and Potential Therapeutic Strategies: A Comprehensive Review
Alpha-Synuclein: Multiple pathogenic roles in trafficking and proteostasis pathways in Parkinson's disease

records.limitations: A molecular trigger described in reviews does not define a person-level latent-state coupling. The Pr construct is broader than alpha-synuclein abundance; direction and effect size require disease-specific experimental and longitudinal support.

records.mechanism_summary: Review-level evidence links activated microglia and astrocytes, inflammatory cytokines, and reactive oxygen species with neuronal oxidative stress and selective neuronal vulnerability in Parkinson disease. I-to-N is retained as a provisional candidate direction.

references.title: Parkinson Disease Signaling Pathways, Molecular Mechanisms, and Potential Therapeutic Strategies: A Comprehensive Review
Key genes and convergent pathogenic mechanisms in Parkinson disease

records.limitations: Inflammation is context-, region-, and stage-dependent and may include protective responses. N is defined as preserved integrity, so any future coefficient sign must be empirically and biologically validated.

records.mechanism_summary: Parkinson disease reviews identify mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress as convergent mechanisms associated with vulnerability and degeneration of dopaminergic neurons. M-to-N is recorded as a provisional mechanism direction.

references.title: Key genes and convergent pathogenic mechanisms in Parkinson disease
Cell biology of Parkinson's disease: Mechanisms of synaptic, lysosomal, and mitochondrial dysfunction

records.limitations: M aggregates multiple metabolic subdomains. Mitochondrial dysfunction is not equivalent to a global metabolic score, and this review-level direction is not a fitted causal parameter.

records.mechanism_summary: Alpha-synuclein aggregation and disruption of multiple proteostasis pathways are repeatedly described in Parkinson disease and are associated with neuronal pathology. Pr-to-N is retained as a candidate direction linking impaired protein quality control with neuronal integrity loss.

references.title: Alpha-Synuclein: Multiple pathogenic roles in trafficking and proteostasis pathways in Parkinson's disease

records.limitations: Alpha-synuclein pathology is not a direct measurement of the entire proteostasis system. The relationship is heterogeneous across cell types and disease subgroups; no coefficient or sign is provided.
